items.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I love Bucky’s, he’s got this little — [INTERVIEWEE] The Jazz Cat. Or which one?

ctx.x: That’s right. That’s correct. And I love the gigs like two weeks ago a fellow said, “Just bring an acoustic guitar.” And I said wow, I haven’t had this in a long time, not even an amp, just an acoustic guitar. Oh that was great. And then there are some where I just bring a small amp and I bring that little, the smallest amp I have.
I love Bucky’s, he’s got this little —
The Jazz Cat. Or which one?

items.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: even Bucky says it to me that you don’t have to play ... Bucky was involved on that ... I got on a few of those ... I would have to replace like with Tony Hatch with

ctx.x: And I sort of miss that these days.

I do too. Because he would play chord melody, he’d play single note melody and of course he would play, if you listen to Johnny Mathis you’ll hear the first thump— I don’t know if Bucky Pizzarelli ever told you that — what we call the thump on the rhythm, and that’s how Johnny Mathis’ records, that was Tony Mottola playing rhythm. Unbelievable. Because guitar, if you play a record, we call a record, CDs today, when you played a record and you’ll say, “Can you hear the guitar” to a layman. He’ll say, “I don’t hear…
Is it a four thumps per measure or is it more of a two and four?
